---
title: "Doctoral projects"
---

I currently supervise four doctoral candidates, and I have room for more within
**EXCURSE** — *Muscle Excursion Range in Strength Training: Implications for Performance
and Injury Prevention* (2025–2028), which I co-lead with Xavier Peirau Terès. That project
is where the funding, the timeline and the laboratory infrastructure already exist, so it
is the most realistic entry point.

## What a project with me looks like

The work sits at the intersection of exercise physiology and applied statistics. In
practice that means a substantial part of any thesis I supervise is measurement and
modelling: how the response is quantified, how the time course is modelled, and what the
data will not support.

I expect candidates to end up able to defend their own analysis, not to outsource it.

## What I look for

- Comfort with quantitative work, or a clear intention to become comfortable. R is the
  working language in my group.
- Willingness to write. A thesis that is not written as it goes is a thesis that stalls.
- Interest in why a method fails, not only in whether the result is significant.

Prior publications are not a requirement.

## Topics currently open

Within EXCURSE: muscle excursion range in strength training, and inter- and
intra-individual variability in the response to strength training.

Adjacent topics I would consider, given the right candidate: post-exercise kinetics of
cardiac biomarkers in young athletes, and validation of field-based performance tests.
